description:
Project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics

Redwood Inference’s Console & Rollouts experience is strong for latency/cost SLOs, but teams still struggle to measure *quality* regressions (answer correctness, safety, instruction following) during model/version/config rollouts without risking user-visible impact. This project adds a “shadow traffic” capability: duplicate a sampled subset of production requests to one or more candidate variants (new model version, quantization profile, routing policy, prompt template), score the shadow outputs asynchronously, and surface quality metrics alongside latency/cost/error metrics—without changing the user’s response.

Goals
- Enable shadow testing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private routing policies: send mirrored requests to shadow variants while returning the control response to the user.
- Capture quality metrics at scale with minimal overhead: store prompts/contexts safely, run async evaluation/scoring (model-graded + heuristic checks), and compute statistically meaningful deltas.
- Integrate with Unified Rollouts/A-B framework: reuse existing experiment and rollout primitives (variant assignment, sampling, guardrails) and attach quality signals to rollback/canary decisions.
- Provide Console UX + APIs for results: per-route/model dashboards, experiment drilldowns, confidence intervals, and regression alerts.

Non-goals (initially)
- Full offline replay system for arbitrary historical traffic beyond short retention windows.
- Customer-managed custom eval code execution inside Redwood (v1 focuses on Redwood-provided metrics and “bring your prompt set” support via eval-harness).

Scope / Workstreams
1) Control plane + routing integration (Platform Control Plane + Smart Routing)
- New “shadow policy” config attached to routes/rollouts: sampling %, shadow targets, headers/metadata behavior, and fail-open rules.
- Deterministic request fingerprinting and variant bucketing for consistent comparisons.

2) Telemetry + data pipelines (Telemetry & Analytics Platform + Observability)
- New event types for shadow request/response pairs, with strict cardinality controls.
- Storage/retention strategy: redact/transform sensitive fields; default short retention; configurable for Dedicated/Private.

3) Evals/scoring subsystem (Applied ML / Performance & Evals)
- Metric definitions (e.g., refusal rate, format adherence, faithfulness proxies, rubric scores), calibration, and statistical methodology.
- Integration with eval-harness for prompt-set-based scoring and model-graded evaluation templates.

4) Console + developer experience (Console & Tooling + DevEx)
- Console pages for “Shadow Experiments” and “Quality deltas” attached to rollouts.
- Public/internal APIs and docs for enabling shadow testing and interpreting results.

5) Reliability, safety, and compliance (SRE + Security)
- Guardrails to ensure shadowing can’t impact tail latency, quotas, or downstream systems.
- Auditability, data minimization, and controls for regulated customers.

Stakeholders (primary)
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (Rollout policies/telemetry requirements)
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & Tooling), Chloe Martin / Jada Williams (Console backend rollouts), Ethan Park / Benji Okafor (Control plane), Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon (Smart Routing), Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (Telemetry)
- Applied ML/Evals: Jonas Weber / Karthik Iyer, Selene Huang, Sana Farid
- Reliability/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant

Milestones / timeline (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): Requirements + architecture + ADRs; define metric set + retention policy
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): Shadow routing MVP + telemetry events + basic scoring pipeline; internal dogfood
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): Console views + alerting + rollout integration; limited beta (select Dedicated customers)
- Phase 3 (4–6 weeks): Hardening (overhead, safety, data controls), docs, GA launch and enablement

Key constraints
- Must not affect user responses and must be “fail open” (if shadow path fails, user path remains healthy).
- Strict cost/overhead budgets (GPU/CPU) for scoring and telemetry.
- Data handling: minimize prompt retention, allow redaction, ensure auditability, support Private deployment constraints.

files.description: PRD for Shadow Traffic tool: user problems, personas (ML eng, platform eng), in-scope metrics, success criteria, rollout plan, pricing/packaging assumptions, and beta customer selection.
Console UX spec for creating/viewing shadow experiments: flows, permissions, drilldowns (delta charts, confidence bands), and how quality signals attach to rollouts.
ADR comparing routing implementation options (inline mirroring vs async replay), deterministic bucketing strategy, and fail-open behavior; includes decision and consequences.
ADR defining telemetry event schemas for shadow pairs, required dimensions, and cardinality limits; includes guidance for tags/labels to avoid metric blowups.
Service overview for control-plane policy support: API surface, config validation, storage, migrations, and integration points with routing and rollouts.
Operational runbook for enabling shadowing safely, monitoring overhead, disabling quickly, and rollback steps if telemetry/scoring pipelines degrade.
SLO/guardrail doc: overhead budgets, acceptable error rates on shadow path, alert thresholds, and what pages vs tickets vs dashboards should be created.
Standard for quality metric naming, sampling math, aggregation windows, confidence interval reporting, and dashboard conventions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Evals spec: initial rubric set (format adherence, safety/refusal, instruction following), model-graded prompts, calibration guidance, and known failure modes.
Data handling policy for shadow traffic artifacts: prompt/response retention, redaction rules, customer opt-outs, and Dedicated/Private configuration knobs.
Working PRD notes: open questions, prioritization, beta customer candidates, and rough sketches of experiment setup UX; links to Linear epics.
Engineering plan broken into milestones and owners (routing, policy config, telemetry, scoring); includes risk register and dependency mapping.
Spreadsheet-style doc listing proposed metrics/dimensions, expected cardinality, and storage costs; includes notes from observability review.
Baseline results from internal replay prompt sets comparing control vs candidate variants; includes early findings and statistical notes.
Draft definitions of quality metrics (what is measured, scoring method, caveats), plus example outputs and rubric iterations.
Draft API contract for Console backend: create experiment, list runs, fetch aggregates, fetch sampled examples; includes pagination and RBAC considerations.
Capacity estimates for ingestion and scoring: expected QPS sampled, CPU/GPU costs, queue sizing, and backpressure strategy.
SRE failure-mode analysis: what happens when scoring is down, when telemetry lags, when shadow targets error; includes mitigations and alerting proposals.
List of config validation scenarios and edge cases (multi-region routes, fallback policies, request types, streaming); intended to become automated tests.
Dashboard mockups and query snippets for quality deltas, segment filters, and time-window comparisons; includes review comments.
Notes on sampling strategies (Bernoulli vs consistent hashing), power calculations, and when to auto-stop experiments.
Draft UI copy for Console: explaining what shadow traffic is, warnings, and guidance on interpreting deltas.
Draft event schema (fields for request fingerprint, control/shadow model IDs, outcome, scoring payload refs) and mapping to storage tables.
Prep doc for security review: data classification, redaction, retention, and access controls; includes unanswered questions and proposed defaults.
Release plan: feature flags, staged rollout to internal tenants, beta gating, and rollback instructions for each component.
Plan for connecting shadow outputs to eval-harness: job format, queueing, rubric versioning, and storage of scored results.
Cost model spreadsheet (represented in text/table form): scoring compute, storage, and incremental telemetry; includes scenarios by sampling rate.
Prototype approaches for redacting prompts (regex rules, structured field allowlists) and notes on false positives/negatives.
QA/E2E test plan for experiment creation, results correctness, permission boundaries, and degraded-mode behaviors.
Collection of real-ish examples where metrics can mislead (format drift, model verbosity changes) and how to interpret/mitigate.
PM ticket tracking PRD completion, stakeholder reviews, and launch criteria; includes links to Confluence PRD and Drive notes.
Define the default metric bundle shipped at launch (rubrics + heuristics), ownership, and versioning policy.
Plan for selecting and onboarding beta customers (Dedicated), including success criteria, comms, and support playbook.
Packaging ticket discussing whether shadow testing is included in base tiers or gated as an add-on; includes cost sensitivity inputs.
Define how quality signals plug into rollout automation (advisory vs automatic rollback), and what thresholds are supported.
Design ticket for Console flow wireframes: create experiment, select variants, view deltas, and drill into examples.
Design ticket for chart components (confidence intervals, segment filters) and visual language for regressions.
Design ticket focused on safety warnings, data retention callouts, and UX around sampling rates and costs.
Implement control-plane schema for shadow policies, validation rules, and migration support; includes sub-issues for edge cases.
Data plane/routing work to mirror a sampled subset of requests to shadow targets with fail-open behavior and timeouts.
Implement stable fingerprinting/bucketing for consistent comparisons and reduced variance across time windows.
Add new telemetry events and ingestion logic for shadow pairs; includes dimension constraints and PII handling.
Build async scoring pipeline (queue, workers, retries, dedupe) to compute rubric metrics for shadow outputs.
Adapter layer to reuse eval-harness scoring templates against shadow outputs; includes rubric version pinning.
Console backend endpoints for shadow experiments: CRUD, aggregates, and example sampling; includes RBAC checks.
Implement Console UI pages and components for viewing shadow experiment deltas and drilldowns.
Define and implement alerts for quality regression thresholds and missing/lagging scoring signals.
Implement hard limits and sampling for high-cardinality tags (prompt_id, customer_id, route) to protect the metrics stack.
Implement redaction and retention: hashed identifiers, prompt truncation/allowlists, configurable retention windows.
Benchmark overhead (p50/p99 latency, CPU) and validate that shadowing does not affect user path SLOs.
Integrate shadow experiments with rollout objects (canary/A-B), linking configurations and exposing results in rollout timeline.
Define and implement mirroring for streaming requests (what gets mirrored, when to stop), with correctness and cost constraints.
Implement backpressure, circuit breaking, and graceful degradation when shadow target/scoring pipeline is unhealthy.
Enable shadow testing for internal tenants, create initial experiments, and track issues found during dogfood.
Add audit log entries for creating/modifying shadow experiments and policy changes; includes permission model updates.
Add SDK bindings (Python/TS/Go) for shadow experiment management APIs and example code.
Create docs and quickstart content: how to enable, choose sampling, interpret metrics, and common pitfalls.
Document and implement Private deployment considerations (local storage, SIEM export, retention defaults, air-gapped scoring options).
